correctness.rationale: Direct closed-neighborhood signature comparison proves the pair-distance-three and no-triple-omission criterion. The step-three cycle bound excludes six-vertex codes: all eleven omitted five-sets violate domination. All 55 independent omitted four-sets are partitioned into five length-eleven translation orbits; three are legal and give 33 minimum codes. Rotational equivariance reduces legal-slide and jump neighbors to three representatives, yielding 11 isolated plus one C22, while the jump rules give four neighbors per state and connectivity. Exhaustive subset enumeration n=4..11 proves no earlier mixed-mobility cycle. Separate standard-library programs independently reproduce the classification and full BFS metrics, including jump radius four and diameter five.

evidence: Code replacement translates to swapping one zero and one one in a labeled binary circular word while preserving unique nonempty length-three detection signatures.
For the eleven-cycle, the omitted vertices must form an independent set of the step-three cycle without three consecutive omissions.
The published 2009 local identifying-code criterion describes feasible words but not exchange adjacency.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Checked cyclic binary necklaces, detector replacement and codeword exchanges as equivalent formulations, not only the code terminology. Feasibility conditions and count of optimal codewords do not logically determine slide-edge connectivity or diameter; no covering move theorem was located.

evidence: Exhaustive exact derivation: the 55 independent omitted four-sets split into five 11-rotation classes, of which exactly three are identifying.
No matching external table of the sliding components 11 isolated and C22 or exact 33-vertex jump graph was found.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: Searches targeted matching numeric invariants and equivalently the orbit word patterns. The 2009 and 2012 optimum cardinality tables are not the same as a complete minimum-configuration transition census. Nonappearance in indexed sources is not a proof that no earlier table exists.

originality.rationale: The radius-one identifying-code definition and optimum code cardinality are prior work; they are explicitly excluded. The new theorem specifies the first mixed slide-mobility order and complete labeled minimum-code transition graphs. In the primary 2009 preprint sections inspected, only local code criteria and scalar optimal sizes are determined. Searches for code migration, exchange, token sliding/jumping, cyclic word equivalents and exact order-eleven tables found no result implying the 11 isolated states plus one 22-cycle, nor the connected 4-regular jump graph. Two highly plausible older full articles were inaccessible beyond their abstracts and remain priority risks; search does not establish historical uniqueness.
residual_risks: Unindexed exchange-graph research on identifying codes or equivalent cyclic binary words may already provide this special case.
Relevant 2004 and 2012 primary full texts were not available for line-by-line inspection.
Independent professional mathematical literature review has not been performed.

value.rationale: Coexistence of frozen optimum codes and locally reconfigurable optimum codes is a natural mobility threshold for sensor relocation at fixed optimal budget. The theorem locates its first possible cycle order, gives the exact component architecture and demonstrates a genuine difference between adjacency-constrained relocation and arbitrary reassignment; these are structural graph properties not inferable from scalar identifying-code numbers alone.
